device_scope: Arduino UNO Q over ADB; device serial intentionally omitted
why_pure_python: numpy is not installed on the board (ModuleNotFoundError), so the optimized runner uses only the standard library.

protocol.note: Two independent runs; medians agree within 1.5%. Values below are run 1, with run 2 in parentheses.

model_shape.quantization: INT8 weights with a per-layer float scale

numerical_agreement.mlp_sparse_int8: ~1.5e-14 on board, 2.13e-14 on x86; float re-association from folding the INT8 scale and the normalisation, NOT a different model
numerical_agreement.warning: This is not zero and must not be reported as zero.

optimizations_applied: int()/float() casts hoisted out of the hot loop (3,025 casts per call removed)
(v - mean) / scale folded to v * a + b: division becomes multiplication, two ops become one
per-layer INT8 weight_scale folded into the weights, removing one multiply per neuron
Python MAC loop replaced by sum(map(mul, weights, itemgetter(*idx)(h))), which runs gather+multiply+accumulate in C
claim_boundary: CPU Python only. No NPU, QNN, Hexagon or GPU acceleration is used or claimed.
Latency is for this UNO Q, this Python build, this replay set only.
Model quality is unchanged by this work: the sparse-INT8 MLP still loses to persistence on the held-out test (0.924 vs 0.806 degC MAE), which is why persistence remains the operational model.
The MLP runs on the board as a labelled challenger, not as the shipped model.
